senses.gloss: m. pl.Carmanians, inhabitants of Carmania, a province of the ancient Persian empire, with the capital Carmana; [oth. opin. (from קִרְמָא) sellers of linen garments; cmp., however, meanings of טַרְסִי I, II].
units: <cite ref="Shabbat 138a">Sabb. 138ᵃ</cite> <he>בדק׳</he> Ms. O. a. Ar. (ed. <he>כדק׳</he>; Ms. M. <he>בדקמינאי</he>) it refers to a folding bed or frame (like that) used by the Carmanians (to exhibit their wares).
<cite ref="Nazir 31b">Naz. 31ᵇ</cite> <he>תורא דקרמנאי</he> an ox of the Carmanians (good for ploughing); <cite ref="Nazir 31b">ib.</cite> <he>דקרמינ׳</he>.—

<cite ref="Bava Kamma 21a:9">B. Kam. 21ᵃ</cite> <he>מעיקרא ק׳ וכ׳</he> originally Carmanians had been living on the abandoned property belonging to the orphans, and had been paying a nominal rent; [Ms. M. <he>קַדְמָאֵי</he>, Ms. R. a. vers. in Raschi <cite ref="S00157"><he>קַדְמוֹנָאֵי</he></cite> old settlers or nomads = <he>בני קדם</he>].
